capabilities: Render a clickable heading TOC for a target file via a ```filecatalog code block in reading view
Insert a TOC with a dual-mode command that replaces a selected [[file]] or inserts a code block frame
Auto-refresh rendered TOC blocks when the target file's headings change
Customize displayed heading levels (H1-H6), colors, font size, line height, and indent
Configure hotkeys by jumping to the native Hotkeys settings page
disambiguation: Not a vault file cataloger; despite the name it generates a table of contents from a document's headings.
extras: README is bilingual (Chinese and English) for community review; the plugin is plain JavaScript with no build step. Static TOC entries use HTML <a> tags, so they are clickable but not tracked by Obsidian and do not update on file rename.
intentEvidence: Replaces DataviewJS filecatalog scripts without Dataview dependency.
motivation: The README says it was built to replace DataviewJS filecatalog scripts and remove the Dataview dependency.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to embed a clickable table of contents of another file inside a note without writing DataviewJS scripts.

relations.evidence: Replaces DataviewJS filecatalog scripts without Dataview dependency.

summary: Heading-based TOC generator that renders a clickable, indented table of contents for any Markdown file via a filecatalog code block or a command.
